title: Objective-C Interop and NSKeyedUnarchiver
platform_conditions: iOS/macOS SDK (Apple frameworks: Foundation NSKeyedUnarchiver, NSPredicate, KVC)
security_mechanism: NSKeyedUnarchiver.unarchiveObject(with:) reconstructs whatever class names the serialized data names; because the archive is attacker-supplied bytes, any class conforming to NSSecureCoding-agnostic NSCoder decoding becomes a deserialization gadget, and Foundation classes with side-effecting initWithCoder implementations have a long history of exploitable use. The typed replacement unarchivedObject(ofClass:from:) refuses classes that do not implement NSSecureCoding, closing the class-confusion hole. The same trust mismatch appears across the ObjC bridge: 'as!' downcasts a bridged AnyObject to a concrete type and traps (or worse, mis-types) when the runtime object differs; KVC setValue(_:forKeyPath:) with an external key path reaches arbitrary setters; NSPredicate(format:) with an interpolated string parses the input as a predicate expression language (injection in its own grammar); String(format:) with an external format string is printf-style format injection.

source_sink_clues.source: Serialized archives from other apps/IPC/pasteboard/network, external strings feeding predicate or format templates, and external key paths.
source_sink_clues.sink: NSKeyedUnarchiver.unarchiveObject(with:); 'as!' on bridged runtime objects; setValue(_:forKeyPath:) with external keys; NSPredicate(format:)/NSExpression(expressionWithFormat:) with interpolated strings; String(format: externalFormat)

tracking_guards: Check deserialization uses NSKeyedUnarchiver.unarchivedObject(ofClass:from:) with an explicit NSSecureCoding class or rejects archives whose classes are not allowlisted; check downcasts use conditional 'as?' with handled failure; check predicate/format strings are built from constants with values bound as arguments (NSPredicate(value:) is still a format — require escaping or constant formats) and key paths come from a fixed allowlist.
not_candidate_when: The archive was produced and consumed inside the same app with no IPC/pasteboard exposure, decoding is constrained to one NSSecureCoding data class of plain properties, or the predicate/format templates are compile-time constants and only argument values are dynamic.
synthetic_safe_example: let obj = try NSKeyedUnarchiver.unarchivedObject(ofClass: SafeClass.self, from: data)
public_references: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html
